2607.28190.title: The MADRS Pipeline: Supporting Depression Assessment in Clinical Trials
2607.28190.paper_summary: Depression is a major mental disorder for which diagnosis relies primarily on clinical assessments. Automated methods to support its detection via the psychiatric MADRS scale are getting more and more attention. While existing solutions primarily focus on detecting the disorder from different text sources (e.g., online text, social media), there is still limited support for clinical trials, where clinical assessments are conducted through structured interviews based on standard guidelines such as SIGMA. In this work, we develop a LLM pipeline specifically designed to support clinicians in supporting the assessment of depression in patients enrolled in clinical trials. Our pipeline converts audio interviews into transcripts, maps them into the ten MADRS symptom items, estimates their severity, and identify problematic clinical ratings associated with them. Evaluation on real clinical interviews shows a strong overall correlation of 0.867 with expert ratings, providing interpretable support for future assessments in clinical trials.
2607.28190.paper_summary_zh: 憂鬱症是一種主要的心理疾病，其診斷主要依賴臨床評估。通過精神病學MADRS量表來支持其檢測的自動化方法正受到越來越多的關注。雖然現有解決方案主要集中在從不同的文本來源（例如，網上文本、社交媒體）檢測該疾病，但對於臨床試驗的支持仍然有限，臨床評估是通過基於標準指導方針（如SIGMA）的結構化訪談進行的。在這項工作中，我們開發了一個專門設計的LLM管道，以支持臨床醫生評估參加臨床試驗的患者的憂鬱症。我們的管道將音頻訪談轉換為文字稿，將其映射到十個MADRS症狀項目，估計其嚴重程度，並識別與之相關的問題臨床評分。對真實臨床訪談的評估顯示，與專家評分之間的整體相關性為0.867，為未來在臨床試驗中的評估提供了可解釋的支持。
